label: Incomplete Task Execution
description: Agent claims completion while key subtasks remain undone.

label: Fabricated References
description: Agent emits code referencing non-existent functions or packages.

label: Stale API Usage
description: Agent uses deprecated or removed APIs.

label: Cascading Error Recovery
description: Agent's fix attempts introduce new errors that compound.

label: Context Window Overflow
description: Important context is truncated; agent drifts.

label: Tool Misinvocation
description: Correct tool, wrong arguments or wrong sequence.

label: Silent Test-Passing Workaround
description: Agent modifies tests or test harness to mask failure.

label: Destructive Action
description: Agent executes rm/force-push/commit bypass without human approval.

label: Goal Drift
description: Agent's working goal diverges from the user's stated goal.

label: Role Violation
description: Agent acts outside its declared role or scope.

label: Task Decomposition Failure
description: Agent fails to break a task into solvable subtasks.

label: Coordination Failure
description: Agents fail to coordinate on shared state or handoff.

label: Redundant Work
description: Multiple agents duplicate effort without coordination.

label: Communication Breakdown
description: Messages between agents are lost, misinterpreted, or ignored.

label: Stalling / Deadlock
description: Agents block waiting on each other with no progress.

label: Premature Termination
description: Agent ends a task before completion criteria are met.

label: Goal Drift
description: Agent's working goal diverges from the user's stated goal.

label: Tool Misuse
description: Agent invokes an available tool incorrectly or unnecessarily.

label: Fabrication in Inter-Agent Messages
description: Agent sends factually incorrect information to another agent.

label: Verification Failure
description: Agent accepts incorrect output without checking.

label: Escalation Failure
description: Agent does not escalate to a human when appropriate.

label: Context Loss
description: Relevant prior context is dropped or truncated.

label: Infinite Loop
description: Agent cycles over the same state or tool call indefinitely.

label: Agent Compromise
description: Unauthorized control or manipulation of an agent; one corrupted node can subvert entire multi-agent workflows.

label: Agent Injection
description: Insertion of malicious instructions into agent prompts, plans, or tool-call arguments.

label: Agent Impersonation
description: Threat actors register counterfeit agents that appear legitimate, tricking other modules into leaking data or executing actions.

label: Agent Flow Manipulation
description: Unauthorized alteration of agent workflow execution paths, e.g., injecting tokens like STOP to reroute workflows or bypass safety logic.

label: Multi-Agent Jailbreaks
description: Jailbreak payload split across agent messages; recombination bypasses single-prompt detectors. Specific to multi-agent topologies.

label: Intra-Agent Responsible AI Concerns
description: Toxic or RAI-violating content propagates through internal inter-agent messages and reaches users or logs without filtering.

label: Bias in Resource Allocation
description: Discriminatory distribution of resources across users when agents act as allocators.

label: Organizational Knowledge Degradation
description: Heavy automation erodes human understanding of the underlying system; recovery is difficult when agents fail.

label: Prioritization Risks (Performance Over Safety)
description: Goal-driven agents skip safety checks to optimize KPIs, prioritizing performance metrics over user safety.

label: Memory Poisoning
description: Attackers embed malicious instructions into long-term memory; every future recall re-executes the attack. Flagship case study in the paper.

label: Cross-Domain Prompt Injection (XPIA)
description: External content (PDFs, calendar invites, web pages) contains hidden commands that hijack agent decision logic.

label: Human-in-the-Loop Bypass
description: Circumvention of human oversight and approval gates.

label: Incorrect Permissions Management
description: Over-scoped agent permissions let agents access files or perform actions beyond the user's intent.

label: Insufficient Isolation
description: Inadequate separation between agent operational boundaries, enabling lateral compromise.

label: Bias Amplification
description: Magnification of existing prejudices in agent outputs across iterative loops.

label: Hallucinations
description: Generation of false or fabricated information, including fabricated tool calls and references.

label: Misinterpretation of Instructions
description: Incorrect understanding of user directives leading to unintended actions.

label: Lack of Transparency
description: Insufficient clarity over agent behavior, preventing informed user consent and oversight.

label: Agent Goal Hijack
description: Attacker-induced diversion of an agent from its user-assigned goal.

label: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
description: Abuse of the agent's tool surface to exceed intended authority.

label: Identity and Privilege Abuse
description: Misuse of agent identities or escalation of privileges.

label: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
description: Compromise via the agent's software, tool, model, or data supply chain, including hallucinated-package-name typosquatting (slopsquatting).

label: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
description: Agent emits or runs code producing unintended remote execution.

label: Memory & Context Poisoning
description: Attacker manipulation of agent memory or long-context state.

label: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
description: Weakly authenticated or validated messages between agents.

label: Cascading Failures
description: Errors that propagate across agent subsystems or the agent fleet.

label: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
description: Social-engineering of humans by or via an agent.

label: Rogue Agents
description: Unsanctioned or self-modifying agents operating outside policy.

label: Agent Cognition and Orchestration
description: Failures in cognitive architecture and control flows unique to agentic systems (83 faults in the sample). Covers LLM integration and agent lifecycle/state.

label: Tooling, Integration, and Actuation
description: Defects in tool invocation and external-system interaction (66 faults). Covers API usage, external connectivity, resource manipulation, coordination, and observability of tool calls.

label: Perception, Context, and Memory
description: Faults in information ingestion, context preservation, and input interpretation (72 faults). Covers persistence and input-interpretation logic.

label: Runtime and Environment Grounding
description: Execution environment, dependency stack, and platform-constraint mismatches (87 faults). The single largest fault dimension by count, dominated by dependency management.

label: System Reliability and Observability
description: Robustness deficiencies and diagnostic challenges in autonomous systems (67 faults). Covers error recovery, UI/visualization, and documentation.

label: LLM Integration Faults
description: Faults in how the agent integrates with its LLM (45 faults).

label: Agent Lifecycle and State
description: Faults in agent startup, execution, termination, and state tracking (38 faults).

label: Tool Execution and API Usage
description: Incorrect or malformed tool/API invocations (17 faults).

label: External Connectivity and Access
description: Connection setup and authentication failures (19 faults).

label: Resource Manipulation
description: Resource-handling and database-misconfiguration faults (16 faults).

label: System Coordination
description: Synchronization errors across components or agents (6 faults).

label: System Observability
description: Logging or telemetry defects (8 faults).

label: Context and State Persistence
description: Memory-persistence and state-load/save failures (12 faults).

label: Input Interpretation and Logic
description: Type handling, validation, encoding, and logic/constraint violations (60 faults).

label: Dependency Management
description: Dependency specification, import resolution, installation, and package resolver/manager failures (67 faults). The single largest major category.

label: Platform Compatibility
description: Environment, platform, API, and integration compatibility mismatches (20 faults).

label: Robustness and Error Recovery
description: Exception-handling and implementation defects (49 faults).

label: UI, Visualization, and Documentation Defects
description: UI defects (13 faults) and documentation defects (5 faults).

label: Dependency and Integration Failures
description: Contract violations between probabilistic artifacts and deterministic interfaces (19.5%).

label: Data and Type Handling Failures
description: Type mismatches and validation gaps (17.6%).

label: Incorrect Token Management
description: Tracking and counting errors affecting context windows.

label: Authentication and Credential Issues
description: Fragile token refresh and credential-expiration handling.

label: Datetime Conversion Errors
description: Inappropriate temporal-value transformations.

label: State Management Defects
description: Inconsistent internal state across interactions.

label: Configuration Inconsistencies
description: Wrong defaults and misconfiguration.

label: API Evolution and Schema Drift
description: Incompatibilities from upstream API changes.

label: Environment-Level Issues
description: Platform-specific constraints and virtual-environment problems.

label: Documentation Gaps
description: Missing or incorrect configuration guidance.

label: Exception Suppression
description: Swallowed errors reducing observability.

label: Ecosystem Fragility
description: Rapid upstream evolution creating tight-coupling vulnerabilities.

label: Accuracy
description: Mitigates hallucinations, misinformation, and disinformation to ensure factually correct outputs.

label: Efficiency
description: Prevents resource-intensive tasks and endless loops; manages cost through dynamic resource management.

label: Privacy
description: Protects against sensitive-data leakage via direct responses or statistical inference.

label: Security
description: Defends against malicious activities and adversarial attacks; preserves data confidentiality and integrity.

label: Safety
description: Prevents harmful or misleading outputs, especially in high-stakes domains.

label: Fairness
description: Addresses bias and discrimination from training data, algorithms, or deployment.

label: Compliance
description: Ensures adherence to legal, regulatory, and industry standards via continuous monitoring.

label: Generalizability
description: Functions effectively across multiple layers and diverse scenarios without per-case configuration.

label: Customizability
description: Tailored protection for specific requirements at different operational layers.

label: Adaptability
description: Adjusts dynamically to varying conditions and emerging threats without manual reconfiguration.

label: Traceability
description: Detailed logs of decision paths, inputs, outputs, and data sources for auditing.

label: Portability
description: Guardrail transfers across FM-based agents with minimal adjustment.

label: Interoperability
description: Functions seamlessly across heterogeneous agents, technologies, and interfaces.

label: Interpretability
description: Provides clarity on how a guardrail operates, enabling user understanding and trust.

label: Prompt Stage
description: Incoming user queries analyzed for harmful content and safety alignment before processing.

label: Intermediate Results Stage
description: Outputs at workflow stages verified for accuracy and safety before final generation.

label: Final Results Stage
description: Final agent outputs checked for goal alignment and governance compliance.

label: Goals
description: Declared user or task objectives.

label: Context
description: Conversation and session context.

label: Memory
description: Long-term or episodic agent memory.

label: Reasoning
description: Chain-of-thought and intermediate reasoning traces.

label: Plans
description: Multi-step action plans produced by the agent.

label: Workflows
description: End-to-end orchestrated task flows.

label: Tools
description: External callable tools and APIs.

label: Knowledge Bases
description: Retrieval corpora and structured knowledge stores.

label: Other Agents
description: Peer or subordinate agents in a multi-agent system.

label: Foundation Models
description: The underlying LLM / FM itself.

label: Block
description: Prevent the action from executing.

label: Filter
description: Strip disallowed content before forwarding.

label: Flag
description: Emit a warning for downstream review.

label: Modify
description: Transform the action or output to a safer variant.

label: Validate
description: Check against a spec or schema before proceeding.

label: Parallel Calls
description: Run multiple checkers concurrently for consensus.

label: Retry
description: Regenerate with adjusted parameters.

label: Fall Back
description: Switch to a safer alternative pathway.

label: Human Intervention
description: Escalate to a human-in-the-loop.

label: Defer
description: Delay the action until conditions are met.

label: Isolate
description: Run the action in a sandbox or quarantined environment.

label: Redundancy
description: Duplicate critical checks for defense in depth.

label: Evaluate
description: Score against metrics before acting.
